title.en: Volume 53 Biographies 3: Li Mi, Dan Xiongxin

sentences.zh: 裴寂裴寂，字玄真，蒲州桑泉人也。

translations.literal: Pei Ji. Pei Ji, styled Xuanzhen, was a native of Sangquan in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, styled Xuanzhen, came from Sangquan in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖融，司本大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rong was Director of the Ward in the Bureau of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rong served as Director of the Ward in the Bureau of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 父瑜，絳州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yu was prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寂少孤，為諸兄之所鞠養。

translations.literal: Ji was orphaned young and was reared by his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, Ji was raised by his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 年十四，補州主簿。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was appointed prefectural chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was appointed prefectural chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 及長，疏眉目，偉姿容。

translations.literal: When grown, his brows were sparse and his features clear; his bearing was imposing.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he had fine, open features and a striking presence.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，為左親衛。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as Left Imperial Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui's Kaihuang era he served as a Left Imperial Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 家貧無以自業，每徒步詣京師，經華岳廟，祭而祝曰：「窮困至此，敢修誠謁，神之有靈，鑑其運命。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he had no means to support himself; he often went on foot to the capital. Passing the shrine of Mount Hua, he offered sacrifice and prayed, saying: "Reduced to such distress, I venture this sincere visit; if the spirits have power, regard my fate."
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to make a living, he often walked to the capital. At the Mount Hua shrine he sacrificed and prayed: "I have come to such want that I dare offer this sincere visit—if the spirits are aware, look upon my fate."

sentences.zh: 若富貴可期，當降吉夢。

translations.literal: If wealth and honor may be expected, send an auspicious dream.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune is in store, grant me an auspicious dream.

sentences.zh: 」再拜而去。

translations.literal: " He bowed twice and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and left.

sentences.zh: 夜夢白頭翁謂寂曰：「卿年三十已後方可得志，終當位極人臣耳。

translations.literal: By night he dreamed a white-haired old man told Ji: "Only after you pass thirty will you realize your ambition; in the end you will reach the highest ministerial rank."
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed a white-haired old man said to him: "You will not fulfill your ambitions until after thirty; in the end you will stand at the pinnacle of the court."

sentences.zh: 」後為齊州司戶。

translations.literal: " He afterward became Registrar of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Registrar of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業中，歷侍御史、駕部承務郎、晉陽宮副監。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he successively served as Attending Censor, Vice Director in the Bureau of Imperial Transport, and Deputy Superintendent of Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he held posts as Attending Censor, Vice Director in the Bureau of Imperial Transport, and Deputy Superintendent of Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖留守太原，與寂有舊，時加親禮，每延之宴語，間以博奕，至於通宵連日，情忘厭倦。

translations.literal: Gaozu, holding Taiyuan in garrison, was old friends with Ji and now treated him with special intimacy; he often invited him to feast and talk, sometimes gambling between them, until whole nights and days passed without weariness or satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, garrisoning Taiyuan, was an old acquaintance of Ji and now showed him exceptional favor, often keeping him at feasts and conversation—sometimes gambling—until whole nights and days passed without either man tiring of the other.

sentences.zh: 時太宗將舉義師而不敢發言，見寂為高祖所厚，乃出私錢數百萬，陰結龍山令高斌廉與寂博戲，漸以輸之。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong wished to raise the righteous army but dared not speak; seeing Ji was deeply favored by Gaozu, he spent several million in private funds and secretly won over Longshan Magistrate Gao Binlian to gamble with Ji, gradually losing to him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then wished to raise the righteous army but dared not speak openly. Seeing how heavily Gaozu favored Ji, he spent millions in private funds and secretly enlisted Longshan Magistrate Gao Binlian to gamble with Ji, deliberately losing to him over time.

sentences.zh: 寂得錢既多，大喜，每日從太宗游。

translations.literal: Ji, having won much money, was greatly pleased and every day accompanied Taizong in his outings.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, having won a great deal of money, was delighted and spent his days in Taizong's company.

sentences.zh: 見其歡甚，遂以情告之，寂即許諾。

translations.literal: Seeing him so joyful, Taizong then confided the plan to him; Ji at once promised.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw how pleased Ji was, Taizong confided the plan; Ji promised at once.

sentences.zh: 寂又以晉陽宮人私侍高祖，高祖從寂飲，酒酣，寂白狀曰：「二郎密纘兵馬，欲舉義旗，正為寂以宮人奉公，恐事發及誅，急為此耳。

translations.literal: Ji also had a woman of Jinyang Palace attend Gaozu in private. When Gaozu drank with Ji and was deep in wine, Ji reported the situation, saying: "The Second Lord is secretly gathering troops and horses and intends to raise the righteous banner—precisely because Ji presented palace women to you, sir, fearing exposure and execution, he has acted in haste."
translations.idiomatic: Ji also had a palace woman from Jinyang attend Gaozu privately. One evening, as Gaozu drank with Ji and grew merry, Ji laid out the facts: "The Second Lord is secretly mustering troops and intends to raise the righteous banner. He moved quickly because I gave you palace women—he feared discovery and execution."

sentences.zh: 今天下大亂，城門之外，皆是盜賊。

translations.literal: Now the realm is in great disorder; beyond the city gates all are bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is in chaos; beyond the gates lie nothing but bandits.

sentences.zh: 若守小節，旦夕死亡；

translations.literal: If you cling to petty scruples, you will die before another day passes;
translations.idiomatic: Cling to small proprieties and you die within days;

sentences.zh: 若舉義兵，必得天位。

translations.literal: if you raise the righteous army, you will surely obtain Heaven's throne.
translations.idiomatic: raise the righteous army and you will surely win the throne.

sentences.zh: 眾情已協，公意如何？

translations.literal: The people's will is already united—what is your intention, sir?
translations.idiomatic: The people's will is already united—what say you, sir?

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「我兒誠有此計，既已定矣，可從之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "My son truly has this plan; since it is already settled, you may follow it."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "My son truly has this design. Since it is settled, follow it."

sentences.zh: 」及義兵起，寂進宮女五百人，並上米九萬斛、雜彩五萬段、甲四十萬領，以供軍用。

translations.literal: " When the righteous army rose, Ji presented five hundred palace women and also submitted ninety thousand bushels of grain, fifty thousand lengths of variegated silks, and four hundred thousand suits of armor to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Ji presented five hundred palace women and also supplied ninety thousand bushels of grain, fifty thousand lengths of colored silks, and four hundred thousand suits of armor for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，以寂為長史，賜爵聞喜縣公。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Directorate was established, Ji was made Chief Clerk and enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's Directorate was established, Ji was appointed Chief Clerk and enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 從至河東，屈突通拒守，攻之不下，三輔豪傑歸義者日有千數。

translations.literal: He followed to Hedong; Qu Tutong held out in defense and could not be taken, while heroes of the three metropolitan districts who submitted to the cause numbered thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the army to Hedong. Qu Tutong held the city and could not be taken, while heroes of the three metropolitan districts submitted by the thousands each day.

sentences.zh: 高祖將先定京師，議者恐通為後患，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished first to secure the capital; advisers feared Tutong as a threat in the rear and hesitated, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wished to secure the capital first, but advisers feared Qu Tutong as a threat from the rear and hesitated.

sentences.zh: 寂進說曰：「今通據蒲關，若不先平，前有京城之守，後有屈突之援，此乃腹背受敵，敗之道也。

translations.literal: Ji advanced counsel, saying: "Now Tutong holds Tong Pass; if he is not pacified first, ahead lies the capital's defense and behind lies Tutong's support—this is being struck front and rear, the way to defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Ji urged: "Qu Tutong holds Tong Pass. Unless we pacify him first, we face the capital ahead and his support behind—attacked front and rear, the road to defeat."

sentences.zh: 未若攻蒲州，下之而後入關。

translations.literal: Better to attack Pu Prefecture, take it, and then enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take Pu Prefecture first, then enter the passes.

sentences.zh: 京師絕援，可不攻而定矣。

translations.literal: With the capital cut off from aid, it may be secured without attack.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from aid, the capital can be taken without a siege.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "That is wrong."

sentences.zh: 兵法尚權，權在於速。

translations.literal: In warfare flexibility is prized; flexibility lies in speed.
translations.idiomatic: Warfare prizes flexibility, and flexibility lies in speed.

sentences.zh: 宜乘機早渡，以駭其心。

translations.literal: We should seize the moment and cross early to shake their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: We should cross early while the chance remains and shake their resolve.

sentences.zh: 我若遲留，彼則生計。

translations.literal: If we delay, they will devise plans.
translations.idiomatic: Delay, and they will find a plan.

sentences.zh: 且關中群盜，所在屯結，未有定主，易以招懷，賊附兵強，何城不克？

translations.literal: Moreover, bandits throughout Guanzhong are encamped everywhere with no settled master; they are easy to win over. With rebels attached, our army grows strong—what city will not fall?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, bandits throughout Guanzhong camp everywhere without a settled leader; they are easy to win over. With rebels joining us our force grows—what city will not fall?

sentences.zh: 屈突通自守賊耳，不足為虞。

translations.literal: Qu Tutong is merely a bandit holding his own ground—not worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tutong is only a bandit holding his ground—not worth worrying over.

sentences.zh: 若失入關之機，則事未可知矣。

translations.literal: If we miss the chance to enter the passes, the outcome cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Miss the chance to enter the passes and the outcome is uncertain.

sentences.zh: 」高祖兩從之，留兵圍河東，而引軍入關。

translations.literal: " Gaozu followed both counsels: he left troops to besiege Hedong and led the army into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took both counsels: he left troops to besiege Hedong and led the main force through the passes.

sentences.zh: 及京師平，賜良田千頃、甲第一區、物四萬段，轉大丞相府長史，進封魏國公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was granted a thousand qing of fertile fields, one first-rank mansion, and forty thousand lengths of goods; he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Grand Chancellor's Directorate, advanced to Duke of Wei with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell he received a thousand qing of fertile land, a first-rank mansion, and forty thousand lengths of goods; he became Chief Clerk of the Grand Chancellor's Directorate and was advanced to Duke of Wei with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及隋恭帝遜位，高祖固讓不受，寂勸進，又不答。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong of Sui abdicated, Gaozu firmly declined and would not accept; Ji urged him to advance, and again he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui's Emperor Gong abdicated, Gaozu firmly refused the throne; Ji urged him to accept, and again he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 寂請見曰：「桀、紂之亡，亦各有子，未聞湯、武臣輔之，可為龜鏡，無所疑也。

translations.literal: Ji requested an audience and said: "The fall of Jie and Zhou each had sons; one never heard that Tang and Wu had ministers assist them—this may serve as a mirror; there is nothing to doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Ji requested audience and said: "Jie and Zhou each had heirs when they fell; Tang and Wu had no ministers propping up fallen tyrants—let that be your mirror. There is nothing to doubt."

sentences.zh: 寂之茅土、大位，皆受之於唐，陛下不為唐帝，臣當去官耳。

translations.literal: Ji's fief and high office were all received from Tang; if Your Majesty will not be Emperor of Tang, your servant must leave office."
translations.idiomatic: "My fief and high rank all came from Tang. If Your Majesty will not be Emperor of Tang, I must resign."

sentences.zh: 」又陳符命十餘事，高祖乃從之。

translations.literal: " He also presented more than ten signs of mandate, and Gaozu then assented.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented more than ten portents of the mandate, and Gaozu at last assented.

sentences.zh: 寂出，命太常具禮儀，擇吉日。

translations.literal: Ji withdrew and ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to prepare the rites and choose an auspicious day.
translations.idiomatic: Ji withdrew and ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to prepare the rites and choose an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 高祖既受禪，謂寂曰：「使我至此，公之力也。

translations.literal: After Gaozu received the abdication, he told Ji: "That I have come to this is your strength."
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne he told Ji: "That I stand here is your doing."

sentences.zh: 」拜尚書右僕射，賜以服玩不可勝紀，仍詔尚食奉御，每日賜寂御膳。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs and given dress and curios beyond counting; he was also ordered that the Imperial Food Service should daily present Ji with the imperial meal.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs and given dress and curios beyond counting; the Imperial Food Service was ordered to send him the imperial meal every day.

sentences.zh: 高祖視朝，必引與同坐，入閣則延之臥內，言無不從，呼為裴監而不名。

translations.literal: Whenever Gaozu held court he always had Ji sit beside him; entering the inner apartments he received him in the sleeping chamber—no word of his was refused—and called him Supervisor Pei without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gaozu held court he seated Ji beside him; in the inner quarters he received him in the sleeping chamber and refused none of his words, calling him Supervisor Pei without using his name.

sentences.zh: 當朝貴戚，親禮莫與為比。

translations.literal: Among the great kin of the court, none was treated with such intimate honor.
translations.idiomatic: Among the great kin at court, none received such intimate honor.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，劉武周將黃子英、宋金剛頻寇太原，行軍總管姜寶誼、李仲文相次陷沒，高祖患之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, Liu Wuzhou's generals Huang Ziying and Song Jingang repeatedly raided Taiyuan; campaigning generals Jiang Baoyi and Li Zhongwen fell in succession, and Gaozu was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 2, Liu Wuzhou's generals Huang Ziying and Song Jingang repeatedly raided Taiyuan; campaigning generals Jiang Baoyi and Li Zhongwen were lost in turn, and Gaozu was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 寂自請行，因為晉州道行軍總管，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Ji volunteered to go and was therefore made Commander on the Jinzhou Route with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Ji volunteered for the campaign and was made Commander on the Jinzhou Route with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 師次介休，而金剛據城以抗寂。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Jiexiu, Jingang held the city to resist Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jiexiu while Jingang held the city against him.

sentences.zh: 寂保於度索原，營中乏水，賊斷其澗路，由是危迫。

translations.literal: Ji encamped on Dusuo Plain; the camp lacked water and the enemy cut his stream route, so that he was in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Ji encamped on Dusuo Plain. The camp ran short of water; the enemy cut his water route and he was driven to extremity.

sentences.zh: 欲移營就水，賊因犯之，師遂大潰，死散略盡。

translations.literal: When he wished to move camp toward water, the enemy attacked; the army was utterly routed and the dead and scattered were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: When he tried to move camp toward water the enemy struck; the army collapsed and nearly all were killed or scattered.

sentences.zh: 寂一日一夜馳至晉州。

translations.literal: Ji rode day and night to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rode day and night to Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以東城鎮俱沒，金剛進逼絳州，寂抗表陳謝，高祖慰諭之，復令鎮撫河東之地。

translations.literal: Because the eastern garrison towns were all lost and Jingang pressed on Jiang Prefecture, Ji submitted a memorial of apology; Gaozu comforted him and again ordered him to pacify the lands east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: With the eastern garrison towns lost and Jingang pressing Jiang Prefecture, Ji submitted a memorial of apology. Gaozu comforted him and again ordered him to pacify the lands east of the River.

sentences.zh: 寂性怯，無捍禦之才，唯發使絡繹，催督虞、秦二州居人，勒入城堡，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: Ji was timid by nature and lacked talent for defense; he only sent messengers in unbroken succession to press the people of Yu and Qin prefectures into fortresses and burn their stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was timid by nature and lacked defensive talent; he only sent messengers in endless succession to drive the people of Yu and Qin into fortresses and burn their stored grain.

sentences.zh: 百姓惶駭，復思為亂。

translations.literal: The people were terrified and again thought of revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The people were terrified and again turned toward rebellion.

sentences.zh: 夏縣人呂崇茂遂殺縣令舉兵反，引金剛為援，寂擊之，復為崇茂所敗。

translations.literal: Lü Chongmao of Xia County then killed the magistrate and raised troops in revolt, drawing Jingang as ally; Ji attacked him and was again defeated by Chongmao.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chongmao of Xia County killed the magistrate and rebelled, calling in Jingang; Ji attacked and was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 被徵入朝，高祖數之曰：「義舉之始，公有翼佐之勳，官爵亦極矣。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, Gaozu reproached him, saying: "At the start of the righteous rising you had merit in aiding the enterprise, and your rank and rewards were already at the limit."
translations.idiomatic: Called to court, Gaozu reproached him: "At the founding of our cause you had merit as ally; your rank and rewards were already at the limit."

sentences.zh: 前拒武周，兵勢足以破敵，致此喪敗，不獨愧於朕乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, facing Wuzhou, your force was enough to break the enemy—yet you brought this ruin. Are you not ashamed before me alone?
translations.idiomatic: "Facing Wuzhou your force was enough to break the enemy, yet you brought this disaster. Are you not ashamed before me?"

sentences.zh: 」以之屬吏，尋釋之，顧待彌重。

translations.literal: " He was handed to the officials, then soon released; his regard and treatment grew still heavier.
translations.idiomatic: He was handed to the judiciary, then soon released; Gaozu's favor toward him grew even heavier.

sentences.zh: 高祖有所巡幸，必令居守。

translations.literal: Whenever Gaozu went on tour he always ordered Ji to remain in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gaozu traveled he left Ji in charge at the capital.

sentences.zh: 麟州刺史韋雲起告寂謀反，訊之無端。

translations.literal: Lin Prefecture Inspector Wei Yunqi reported that Ji was plotting rebellion; on investigation there was no basis.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Prefecture Inspector Wei Yunqi reported Ji for plotting rebellion; inquiry found no basis.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂寂曰：「朕之有天下者，本公所推，今豈有貳心？

translations.literal: Gaozu told Ji: "That I possess the realm was originally pushed forward by you—how could I now have a second heart?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Ji: "That I hold the realm was originally your doing—how could I now doubt you?

sentences.zh: 皁白鬚分，所以推究耳。

translations.literal: Black and white must be separated—that is why the matter was pursued."
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong must be separated—that is why it was investigated."

sentences.zh: 」因令貴妃三人齎珍饌、寶器就寂第，宴樂極歡，經宿而去。

translations.literal: " He then ordered three imperial consorts to carry delicacies and treasures to Ji's residence; they feasted in utmost joy and departed only after spending the night.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent three imperial consorts with delicacies and treasures to Ji's house; they feasted through the night and left at dawn.

sentences.zh: 又嘗從容謂寂曰：「我李氏昔在隴西，富有龜玉，降及祖祢，姻婭帝室。

translations.literal: He also once said to Ji at leisure: "Our Li clan of old in Longxi was rich in tortoise and jade; descending to my ancestors and father, we married into the imperial house."
translations.idiomatic: He also once said to Ji in private: "Our Li of Longxi once possessed tortoise and jade in abundance; my ancestors and father married into the imperial clan."

sentences.zh: 及舉義兵，四海雲集，才涉數日，升為天子。

translations.literal: When we raised the righteous army, the realm gathered like clouds; within only a few days I ascended as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When we raised the righteous army the realm gathered like clouds; within days I became Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 至如前代皇王，多起微賤，劬勞行陣，下不聊生。

translations.literal: As for former dynasties' kings, most rose from humble stations, toiling in the ranks while those below could not live.
translations.idiomatic: Former dynasties' kings mostly rose from humble stations, toiling in the ranks while the people could not live.

sentences.zh: 公復世胄名家，歷職清顯，豈若蕭何、曹參起自刀筆吏也！

translations.literal: You, sir, are again of a noble clan and famous house, holding clear and eminent posts through successive offices—how can you be compared to Xiao He and Cao Shen, who rose from clerks with writing knives!
translations.idiomatic: You are of a noble house with eminent posts—how can you be compared to Xiao He and Cao Shen, who rose from clerks with writing knives!

sentences.zh: 唯我與公，千載之後，無愧前修矣。

translations.literal: Only you and I, a thousand years hence, will have no cause to blush before the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Only you and I, a thousand years hence, need not blush before the ancients."

sentences.zh: 」其年，改鑄錢，特賜寂令自鑄造。

translations.literal: That year coinage was recast and Ji was specially permitted to cast his own.
translations.idiomatic: That year the coinage was recast and Ji was specially allowed to cast his own.

sentences.zh: 又為趙王元景聘寂女為妃。

translations.literal: He also had Ji's daughter taken as consort for Prince Yuanjing of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Ji's daughter marry Prince Yuanjing of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷尚書左僕射，賜宴於含章殿，高祖極歡，寂頓首而言曰：「臣初發太原，以有慈旨，清平之後，許以退耕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs and given a feast in the Hall of Contained Elegance; Gaozu was exceedingly merry and Ji bowed his head and said: "When I first set out from Taiyuan there was a gracious decree that after peace was secured I might retire to farming."
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became Left Vice Minister and was feasted in the Hall of Contained Elegance. Gaozu was exceedingly merry; Ji bowed and said: "When I left Taiyuan Your Majesty promised that after peace I might retire to the fields."

sentences.zh: 今四海乂安，伏願賜臣骸骨。

translations.literal: Now the realm is at peace within the four seas; I venture to beg leave of my bones."
translations.idiomatic: "Now the realm is at peace; I beg to be released from service."

sentences.zh: 」高祖泣下沾襟曰：「今猶未也，要相偕老耳。

translations.literal: Gaozu wept until his robe was wet and said: "Not yet— we must grow old together."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wept until his robe was wet: "Not yet—we must grow old together."

sentences.zh: 公為台司，我為太上，逍遙一代，豈不快哉！

translations.literal: You, sir, will be Chancellor of the Directorate; I will be Retired Emperor—we shall roam through an age: could it not be joyous!
translations.idiomatic: "You will head the Directorate; I will be Retired Emperor—we shall roam through an age together. What could be happier!"

sentences.zh: 」俄冊司空，賜實封五百戶，遣尚書員外郎一人每日更直寂第，其見崇貴如此。

translations.literal: " Shortly he was enfeoffed as Minister of Works with an added substantive fief of five hundred households; an Outer Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs was sent daily in rotation to Ji's residence—such was the honor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was made Minister of Works with five hundred added households; an official of the Department was sent daily in rotation to his house—such was the honor he received.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，加實封並前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan his substantive fief was increased to one thousand five hundred households including the previous total.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 1 his substantive fief rose to fifteen hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 二年，太宗祠南郊，命寂與長孫無忌同升金輅，寂辭讓，太宗曰：「以公有佐命之勳，無忌亦宣力於朕，同載參乘，非公而誰？

translations.literal: In the second year, when Taizong sacrificed at the Southern Altars, he ordered Ji and Zhangsun Wuji to ascend the golden carriage together; Ji declined, and Taizong said: "For your merit in aiding the founding, and Wuji's service to me—sharing the carriage as companions-in-chief—if not you, then who?
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, when Taizong sacrificed at the Southern Altars, he ordered Ji and Zhangsun Wuji to ride the golden carriage together. Ji declined; Taizong said: "You aided the founding; Wuji has served me—who but you two should share this carriage?"

sentences.zh: 」遂同乘而歸。

translations.literal: " They then rode back together.
translations.idiomatic: They rode back together.

sentences.zh: 三年，有沙門法雅，初以恩幸出入兩宮，至是禁絕之，法雅怨望，出妖言，伏法。

translations.literal: In the third year there was the monk Fayi, who at first through favor moved in and out of both palaces; now he was forbidden access. Fayi harbored resentment and spread demonic talk and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the monk Fayi, who had once enjoyed favor in both palaces, was barred from access. He harbored resentment, spread seditious talk, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書杜如晦鞫其獄，法雅乃稱寂知其言，寂對曰：「法雅惟云時候方行疾疫，初不聞妖言。

translations.literal: Minister of War Du Ruhui investigated the case; Fayi then said Ji knew his words, and Ji replied: "Fayi only said pestilence would soon run through the seasons; at first I never heard demonic talk."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Du Ruhui investigated; Fayi said Ji knew his words. Ji replied: "Fayi only said pestilence would soon spread—I never heard seditious talk."

sentences.zh: 」法雅證之，坐是免官，削食邑之半，放歸本邑。

translations.literal: Fayi bore witness against him; for this Ji was removed from office and half his fief was cut; he was sent back to his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fayi testified against him; Ji was dismissed and half his fief was cut; he was sent to his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 寂請住京師，太宗數之曰：「計公勳庸，不至於此，徒以恩澤，特居第一。

translations.literal: Ji asked to remain in the capital; Taizong reproached him: "Considering your merit, it should not have come to this—only through favor did you occupy the first place."
translations.idiomatic: Ji asked to stay in the capital. Taizong reproached him: "By merit alone you should not stand first—only old favor placed you there."

sentences.zh: 武德之時，政刑紕繆，官方弛紊，職公之由。

translations.literal: In Wude times government and punishments were tangled and officialdom lax and disorderly—much of it was your doing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude, government and punishments were tangled and offices lax—much of that was your doing.

sentences.zh: 但以舊情，不能極法，歸掃墳墓，何得復辭？

translations.literal: But for old affection I cannot punish you to the full; go sweep your ancestors' tombs—how can you refuse again?
translations.idiomatic: For old affection I will not punish you fully. Go sweep your ancestors' tombs—will you refuse again?

sentences.zh: 」寂遂歸蒲州。

translations.literal: " Ji then returned to Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji returned to Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有狂人自稱信行，寓居汾陰，言多妖妄，常謂寂家僮曰：「裴公有天分。

translations.literal: Before long a madman calling himself Xinxing lodged at Fenyin and spoke much that was demonic and false, often telling Ji's household slave: "Lord Pei has Heaven's portion."
translations.idiomatic: Soon a madman calling himself Xinxing lodged at Fenyin and spoke wildly, often telling Ji's slave: "Lord Pei has Heaven's portion."

sentences.zh: 」於時信行已死，寂監奴恭命以其言白寂，寂惶懼不敢聞奏，陰呼恭命殺所言者。

translations.literal: By then Xinxing was dead; Ji's overseer slave Gongming used his words to inform Ji; Ji was afraid and dared not report, but secretly ordered Gongming to kill the speaker.
translations.idiomatic: Xinxing was already dead; Ji's overseer Gongming repeated the words to Ji. Ji was afraid and dared not report it, but secretly ordered Gongming to kill the man who had spoken.

sentences.zh: 恭命縱令亡匿，寂不知之。

translations.literal: Gongming let him escape and hide; Ji did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongming let the man escape; Ji did not know.

sentences.zh: 寂遣恭命收納封邑，得錢百餘萬，因用而盡。

translations.literal: Ji sent Gongming to collect and seal the revenues of his fief and obtained more than a million cash, which he then spent entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent Gongming to collect his fief revenues—more than a million cash—which he then spent entirely.

sentences.zh: 寂怒，將遣人捕之，恭命懼而上變。

translations.literal: Ji was angry and was about to send men to arrest him; Gongming, in fear, reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ji grew angry and was about to arrest him; Gongming, in fear, reported everything.

sentences.zh: 太宗大怒，謂侍臣曰：「寂有死罪者四：位為三公而與妖人法雅親密，罪一也；

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly angered and told the attendants: "Ji has four capital crimes: holding rank as one of the Three Dukes yet intimate with the demonic man Fayi—crime one;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was furious and told his attendants: "Ji has four capital crimes: as one of the Three Dukes he was intimate with the seditious monk Fayi—first;

sentences.zh: 事發之後，乃負氣憤怒，稱國家有天下，是我所謀，罪二也；

translations.literal: after the affair broke out he bore resentment in anger, saying the realm was won by my plotting—crime two;
translations.idiomatic: after the affair he spoke in angry resentment, saying the realm was won by his plotting—second;

sentences.zh: 妖人言其有天分，匿而不奏，罪三也；

translations.literal: the demonic man said he had Heaven's portion and he concealed it without reporting—crime three;
translations.idiomatic: the madman said he had Heaven's portion and he concealed it—third;

sentences.zh: 陰行殺戮以滅口，罪四也。

translations.literal: he secretly carried out killings to silence mouths—crime four.
translations.idiomatic: he secretly killed men to silence them—fourth.

sentences.zh: 我殺之非無辭矣。

translations.literal: I would not be without grounds in killing him.
translations.idiomatic: I would not lack grounds to kill him.

sentences.zh: 議者多言流配，朕其從眾乎。

translations.literal: Advisers mostly said exile; shall I follow the multitude?
translations.idiomatic: Advisers mostly urged exile; shall I follow them?

sentences.zh: 」於是徙交州，竟流靜州。

translations.literal: " He was therefore banished to Jiaozhou and in the end was exiled to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to Jiaozhou and ultimately exiled to Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄逢山羌為亂，或言反獠劫寂為主，太宗聞之曰：「我國家於寂有性命之恩，必不然矣。

translations.literal: Soon mountain Qiang raided in disorder; some said the rebel Liao had seized Ji as leader; Taizong heard it and said: "Our state owes Ji the grace of life—surely it cannot be so."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qiang raiders rose; some said rebels had made Ji their leader. Taizong heard it and said: "Our house owes Ji the grace of life—it cannot be."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，果稱寂率家僮破賊。

translations.literal: Before long it proved that Ji had indeed led his household slaves to break the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Ji had led household slaves and broken the bandits.

sentences.zh: 太宗思寂佐命之功，徵入朝，會卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: Taizong, mindful of Ji's merit in aiding the founding, summoned him to court; he happened to die on the way, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his founding merit, Taizong summoned him; he died on the way, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈相州刺史、工部尚書、河東郡公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Prefect of Xiang Prefecture, Minister of Works, and Duke of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Prefect of Xiang, Minister of Works, and Duke of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子律師嗣，尚太宗妹臨海長公主，官至汴州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Lüshi inherited; he married Taizong's younger sister Princess Linhai of the Long Lineage and reached the post of Prefect of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüshi inherited the line, married Princess Linhai, Taizong's younger sister, and rose to Prefect of Bian.

sentences.zh: 律師子承先，則天時為殿中監，為酷吏所殺。

translations.literal: Lüshi's son Chengxian, in the time of Empress Zetian, was Director of the Palace Domestic Service and was killed by the cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lüshi's son Chengxian served as Director of the Palace Domestic Service under Empress Wu and was killed by the secret police.

sentences.zh: 劉文靜劉文靜，字肇仁，自雲彭城人，代居京兆之武功。

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing. Liu Wenjing, styled Zhaoren, claimed descent from Pengcheng; his family had long dwelt at Wugong in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing, styled Zhaoren, claimed descent from Pengcheng; for generations his family lived at Wugong in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖懿用，石州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yiyong was prefect of Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yiyong was prefect of Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父韶，隋時戰沒，贈上儀同三司。

translations.literal: His father Shao died in battle under Sui and was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao died in battle under Sui and was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 少以其父身死王事，襲父儀同三司。

translations.literal: In youth, because his father died in the king's service, he inherited his father's Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, because his father died in the emperor's service, he inherited his father's rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 偉姿儀，有器干，倜儻多權略。

translations.literal: His bearing was imposing, he had capacity and talent, was bold and unconventional and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He had an imposing bearing, real ability, and a bold, unconventional mind full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 隋末，為晉陽令，遇裴寂為晉陽宮監，因而結友。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he was Magistrate of Jinyang; he met Pei Ji as Deputy Superintendent of Jinyang Palace and thus formed a friendship.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui he was Magistrate of Jinyang and befriended Pei Ji, then Deputy Superintendent of Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 夜與同宿，寂見城上烽火，仰天嘆曰：「卑賤之極，家道屢空，又屬亂離，當何取濟？

translations.literal: One night he lodged with Ji; Ji saw beacon fires on the wall and sighed toward Heaven: "At the extreme of low estate, the family path repeatedly empty, and again we meet disorder—how shall we find relief?
translations.idiomatic: One night he lodged with Ji. Ji saw beacon fires on the walls and sighed to Heaven: "Reduced to the lowest estate, our house repeatedly emptied, and now chaos—how shall we find relief?"

sentences.zh: 」文靜笑曰：「世途若此，時事可知。

translations.literal: " Wenjing laughed and said: "The age is like this—the times can be known."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing laughed: "The age is like this—the times tell their own tale."

sentences.zh: 吾二人相得，何患於卑賤？

translations.literal: We two have found each other—what need to fear low estate?
translations.idiomatic: "We two have found each other—why fear low estate?"

sentences.zh: 及高祖鎮太原，文靜察高祖有四方之志，深自結托。

translations.literal: When Gaozu garrisoned Taiyuan, Wenjing perceived that Gaozu harbored ambition for the four quarters and attached himself deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu garrisoned Taiyuan, Wenjing saw his ambition for the realm and attached himself deeply.

sentences.zh: 又竊觀太宗，謂寂曰：「非常人也。

translations.literal: He also secretly observed Taizong and told Ji: "An extraordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: He also studied Taizong in secret and told Ji: "That is no ordinary man."

sentences.zh: 大度類於漢高，神武同於魏祖，其年雖少，乃天縱矣。

translations.literal: His magnanimity resembles Han Gaozu; his martial spirit matches Wei Wudi; though young in years, he is Heaven-sent.
translations.idiomatic: "His breadth resembles Han Gaozu; his martial spirit, Wei Wudi. Young as he is, he is Heaven-sent."

sentences.zh: 」寂初未然之。

translations.literal: Ji at first did not credit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji at first did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 後文靜坐與李密連婚，煬帝令繫於郡獄。

translations.literal: Later Wenjing was imprisoned for contracting marriage with Li Mi; Emperor Yang ordered him held in the commandery prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenjing was imprisoned for ties to Li Mi through marriage; Emperor Yang ordered him held in the commandery jail.

sentences.zh: 太宗以文靜可與謀議，入禁所視之。

translations.literal: Taizong, thinking Wenjing could be taken into counsel, entered the prison to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, believing Wenjing could be enlisted, visited him in prison.

sentences.zh: 文靜大喜曰：「天下大亂，非有湯、武、高、光之才，不能定也。

translations.literal: Wenjing was greatly pleased and said: "The realm is in great disorder; without the talents of Tang, Wu, Han Gaozu, or Guangwu, it cannot be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing was overjoyed and said: "The realm is in chaos. Without men like Tang, Wu, Han Gaozu, or Guangwu it cannot be settled."

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「卿安知無？

translations.literal: Taizong said: "How do you know there are none?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "How do you know there are none?"

sentences.zh: 但恐常人不能別耳。

translations.literal: I only fear ordinary men cannot distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: "I only fear ordinary men cannot tell them apart."

sentences.zh: 今入禁所相看，非兒女之情相憂而已。

translations.literal: That I enter the prison to see you is not merely the affection of children worrying for one another.
translations.idiomatic: "I come to the prison not merely as kin worrying for kin."

sentences.zh: 時事如此，故來與君圖舉大計，請善籌其事。

translations.literal: The times are thus; I have come to plot a great design with you—please plan the matter well.
translations.idiomatic: "The times demand it. I have come to plot a great undertaking with you—plan it well."

sentences.zh: 」文靜曰：「今李密長圍洛邑，主上流播淮南，大賊連州郡、小盜阻澤山者，萬數矣，但須真主驅駕取之。

translations.literal: Wenjing said: "Now Li Mi has long besieged Luoyang; the ruler drifts at Huainan; great bandits link commanderies and counties, small robbers block mountains and marshes—their number is in the tens of thousands; only a true lord need drive and take them."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing said: "Li Mi besieges Luoyang; the emperor drifts at Huainan; great rebels hold commanderies, small bandits the hills—tens of thousands of them. Only a true lord need drive and take them."

sentences.zh: 誠能應天順人，舉旗大呼，則四海不足定也。

translations.literal: If one can accord with Heaven and follow the people, raise the banner and cry aloud, then the four seas are not enough to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: "Answer Heaven and follow the people, raise the banner and cry out—and the four seas are not enough to hold what you take."

sentences.zh: 今太原百姓避盜賊者，皆入此城。

translations.literal: Now the people of Taiyuan fleeing bandits have all entered this city.
translations.idiomatic: "The people of Taiyuan fleeing bandits have all entered this city."

sentences.zh: 文靜為令數年，知其豪傑，一朝嘯集，可得十萬人，尊公所領之兵，復且數萬，君言出口，誰敢不從？

translations.literal: Wenjing has been magistrate several years and knows its bold spirits; at one call they can gather a hundred thousand; the troops your honored father commands are again several tens of thousands; once you speak, who will not follow?
translations.idiomatic: "I have been magistrate for years and know its bold men; one call gathers a hundred thousand. Your father's troops number tens of thousands more. Speak, and who will not follow?"

sentences.zh: 乘虛入關，號令天下，不盈半歲，帝業可成。

translations.literal: Seize the moment and enter the passes; proclaim command over the realm—in less than half a year the imperial enterprise can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: "Strike into the passes, proclaim command over the realm—in half a year the throne can be yours."

sentences.zh: 」太宗笑曰：「君言正合人意。

translations.literal: Taizong laughed and said: "Your words exactly match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong laughed: "Your words match my intent exactly."

sentences.zh: 」於是部署賓客，潛圖起義。

translations.literal: He then deployed retainers and secretly plotted the rising.
translations.idiomatic: He then deployed his men and secretly plotted the uprising.

sentences.zh: 候機當發，恐高祖不從，沉吟者久之。

translations.literal: Waiting for the moment to act, he feared Gaozu would not consent and brooded long.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting for the moment, he feared Gaozu would not consent and brooded for a long time.

sentences.zh: 文靜見高祖厚於裴寂，欲因寂開說，於是引寂交於太宗，得通謀議。

translations.literal: Wenjing saw Gaozu was close to Pei Ji and wished to open persuasion through Ji; he therefore introduced Ji to Taizong and gained access to joint counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing saw how close Gaozu was to Pei Ji and introduced Ji to Taizong so counsel could flow through him.

sentences.zh: 及高君雅為突厥所敗，高祖被拘，太宗又遣文靜共寂進說曰：「《易》稱『知幾其神乎』，今大亂已作，公處嫌疑之地，當不賞之功，何以圖全？

translations.literal: When Gao Junya was defeated by the Turks and Gaozu was detained, Taizong again sent Wenjing with Ji to advance counsel, saying: "The Changes say 'To know the subtle is divine'—now great disorder has begun; you stand in a place of suspicion with unrewarded merit—how will you preserve yourself?
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Junya was defeated by the Turks and Gaozu was detained, Taizong sent Wenjing with Ji to counsel him: "The Changes say to know the subtle is divine. Great disorder has begun; you stand suspected with unrewarded merit—how will you survive?"

sentences.zh: 其裨將敗衄，以罪見歸。

translations.literal: His deputy generals were defeated and he returns under blame.
translations.idiomatic: "His deputies were defeated and he returns under blame."

sentences.zh: 事誠迫矣，當須為計。

translations.literal: The matter is truly urgent; a plan must be made at once.
translations.idiomatic: "The matter is urgent; you must act now."

sentences.zh: 晉陽之地，士馬精強，宮監之中，府庫盈積，以茲舉事，可立大功。

translations.literal: The land of Jinyang has strong soldiers and horses; within the palace superintendent's storehouses are full; with this you may raise a great achievement.
translations.idiomatic: "Jinyang has strong troops; the palace storehouses are full. With this you can achieve greatness."

sentences.zh: 關中天府，代王沖幼，權豪並起，未有適從。

translations.literal: Guanzhong is Heaven's storeroom; the Sui heir is young; powerful clans rise everywhere with no settled allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: "Guanzhong is the empire's storeroom; the Sui heir is a child; powerful clans rise with no settled master."

sentences.zh: 願公興兵西入，以圖大事。

translations.literal: I wish you, sir, to raise troops and march west to pursue the great design.
translations.idiomatic: "Raise troops and march west to seize the great prize."

sentences.zh: 何乃受單使之囚乎？

translations.literal: Why accept imprisonment by a lone envoy?
translations.idiomatic: "Why accept imprisonment by a lone envoy?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖然之。

translations.literal: Gaozu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 時太宗潛結死士，與文靜等協議，剋日舉兵，會高祖得釋而止。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong was secretly binding men willing to die; with Wenjing and others he agreed on a day to raise troops, but when Gaozu was released the plan halted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was secretly binding men willing to die; he and Wenjing fixed a day to rise, but when Gaozu was released the plan halted.

sentences.zh: 乃命文靜詐為煬帝敕，發太原、西河、雁門、馬邑，人年二十已上、五十已下悉為兵，期以歲暮集涿郡，將伐遼東。

translations.literal: He then ordered Wenjing to forge an edict in Emperor Yang's name, mobilizing Taiyuan, Xihe, Yanmen, and Mayi—all men from twenty up to fifty down as soldiers—with assembly at Zhuo Commandery by year's end to campaign against Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wenjing to forge an edict in Emperor Yang's name mobilizing Taiyuan, Xihe, Yanmen, and Mayi—all men twenty to fifty—with assembly at Zhuo by year's end for Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 由是人情大擾，思亂者益眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon popular feeling was greatly disturbed and those who thought of revolt grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Popular feeling was thrown into turmoil and those who wished to rebel grew more numerous.

sentences.zh: 文靜因謂裴寂曰：「公豈不聞『先發制人，後發制於人』乎？

translations.literal: Wenjing therefore said to Pei Ji: "Have you, sir, not heard 'He who strikes first controls others; he who strikes late is controlled by others'?
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing told Pei Ji: "Have you not heard that he who strikes first controls others, and he who strikes late is controlled?"

sentences.zh: 唐公名應圖讖，聞於天下，何乃推延，自貽禍釁？

translations.literal: Lord Tang's name answers the charts and prophecies and is known throughout the realm—why delay and bring calamity on yourself?
translations.idiomatic: "Lord Tang's name answers the prophecies and is known throughout the realm—why delay and invite disaster?"

sentences.zh: 宜早勸唐公，以時舉義。

translations.literal: You should early urge Lord Tang to raise the righteous cause in season.
translations.idiomatic: "Urge Lord Tang early to raise the righteous cause."

sentences.zh: 」又脅寂曰：「且公為宮監，而以宮人侍客，公死可爾，何誤唐公也？

translations.literal: He also coerced Ji, saying: "Moreover you, sir, are palace superintendent yet presented palace women to a guest—your death would be fitting; why implicate Lord Tang?
translations.idiomatic: He also pressed Ji: "You are palace superintendent yet gave palace women to a guest—your death would be fitting. Why drag Lord Tang down with you?"

sentences.zh: 」寂甚懼，乃屢促高祖起兵。

translations.literal: Ji was greatly afraid and repeatedly urged Gaozu to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was terrified and repeatedly urged Gaozu to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 會馬邑人劉武周殺太守王仁恭，自稱天子，引突厥之眾，將侵太原。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou of Mayi killed Prefect Wang Rengong and styled himself Son of Heaven, leading Turk forces to invade Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou of Mayi killed Prefect Wang Rengong and styled himself Son of Heaven, leading Turk forces against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣文靜及長孫順德等分部募兵，以討武周為辭；

translations.literal: Taizong sent Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde and others to raise troops by districts, on the pretext of campaigning against Wuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde to raise troops by districts on the pretext of campaigning against Wuzhou;

sentences.zh: 又令文靜與裴寂偽作符敕，出宮監庫物以供留守資用，因募兵集眾。

translations.literal: he also ordered Wenjing with Pei Ji to forge talisman edicts and issue palace store goods to supply the garrison's needs, thereby gathering troops.
translations.idiomatic: he also ordered Wenjing and Pei Ji to forge talisman edicts and draw on palace stores to supply the garrison and gather troops.

sentences.zh: 及義兵將起，副留守王威、高君雅獨懷猜貳。

translations.literal: When the righteous army was about to rise, Deputy Superintendents Wang Wei and Gao Junya alone harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: As the righteous army was about to rise, Deputy Superintendents Wang Wei and Gao Junya alone harbored suspicion.

sentences.zh: 後數日，將大會於晉祠，威及君雅潛謀害高祖，晉陽鄉長劉世龍以白太宗。

translations.literal: Several days later, when a great assembly was to be held at the Jin Shrine, Wei and Junya secretly plotted to harm Gaozu; Jinyang District Elder Liu Shilong reported it to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Days later, at a great assembly at the Jin Shrine, Wei and Junya plotted to kill Gaozu; District Elder Liu Shilong reported it to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗既知迫急，欲先事誅之，遣文靜與鷹揚府司馬劉政會投急變之書，詣留守告威等二人謀反。

translations.literal: Taizong, knowing the urgency, wished first to execute them and sent Wenjing with Hawk-Promotion Directorate Major Liu Zhenghui to deliver an urgent report accusing Wei and the two of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the urgency, Taizong sent Wenjing with Major Liu Zhenghui of the Hawk-Promotion Directorate to accuse Wei and Junya of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 是日，高祖與威、君雅同坐視事，文靜引政會至庭中，雲有密狀，知人欲反。

translations.literal: That day Gaozu sat with Wei and Junya handling affairs; Wenjing brought Zhenghui to the courtyard, saying there was a secret report and that men wished to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: That day Gaozu sat with Wei and Junya at court; Wenjing brought Zhenghui to the courtyard with a secret report that men wished to rebel.

sentences.zh: 高祖指威等取狀看之，政會不肯與，曰：「所告是副留守事，唯唐公得看之耳。

translations.literal: Gaozu pointed at Wei and the others to take the report and look; Zhenghui would not give it, saying: "What is reported concerns the deputy superintendents—only Lord Tang may view it."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Wei to take the report; Zhenghui refused: "This concerns the deputy superintendents—only Lord Tang may read it."

sentences.zh: 」高祖陽驚曰：「豈有是乎！

translations.literal: Gaozu feigned alarm and said: "How can there be such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu feigned shock: "How can this be!"

sentences.zh: 」覽狀訖，謂威等曰：「此人告公事，如何？

translations.literal: After reading the report through, he said to Wei and the others: "This man reports your affair—what of it?
translations.idiomatic: After reading it he said to Wei and the others: "This man accuses you—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 」君雅大詬曰：「此是反人，欲殺我也！

translations.literal: Junya cursed loudly: "These are rebels who wish to kill me!
translations.idiomatic: Junya cursed: "These are rebels who mean to kill me!"

sentences.zh: 」文靜叱左右執之，囚於別室。

translations.literal: Wenjing shouted for the attendants to seize them and imprisoned them in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing ordered attendants to seize them and held them apart.

sentences.zh: 既拘威等，竟得舉兵。

translations.literal: Once Wei and the others were detained, the army was finally raised.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei and Junya detained, the army rose at last.

sentences.zh: 高祖開大將軍府，以文靜為軍司馬。

translations.literal: Gaozu opened the Grand General's Directorate and made Wenjing Army Major.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu opened the Grand General's Directorate and made Wenjing Army Major.

sentences.zh: 文靜勸改旗幟以彰義舉，又請連突厥以益兵威，高祖並從之。

translations.literal: Wenjing urged changing the banners to proclaim the righteous rising and also asked to ally with the Turks to increase military prestige; Gaozu followed both.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing urged changing the banners to proclaim the cause and allying with the Turks for strength; Gaozu agreed to both.

sentences.zh: 因遣文靜使於始畢可汗，始畢曰：「唐公起事，今欲何為？

translations.literal: He therefore sent Wenjing as envoy to Shibi Khan; Shibi said: "Lord Tang has risen—what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wenjing to Shibi Khan, who asked: "Lord Tang has risen—what do you intend?"

sentences.zh: 」文靜曰：「皇帝廢冢嫡，傳位後主，致斯禍亂。

translations.literal: Wenjing said: "The emperor deposed the legitimate heir and passed the throne to a later lord, bringing this calamitous disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing said: "The emperor deposed the legitimate heir and enthroned a lesser son, bringing this chaos."

sentences.zh: 唐公國之懿戚，不忍坐觀成敗，故起義軍，欲黜不當立者。

translations.literal: Lord Tang is the state's imperial kin; he could not bear to sit and watch success or failure, and therefore raised the righteous army to remove the one unfit to stand.
translations.idiomatic: "Lord Tang is imperial kin; he could not sit idle and therefore raised the army to remove the unfit ruler."

sentences.zh: 願與可汗兵馬同入京師，人眾土地入唐公，財帛金寶入突厥。

translations.literal: I wish to enter the capital with the khan's cavalry and horses; population and land shall go to Lord Tang, wealth, silks, and gold to the Turks."
translations.idiomatic: "Let your cavalry enter the capital with us—population and land to Lord Tang, wealth and gold to the Turks."

sentences.zh: 」始畢大喜，即遣將康鞘利領騎二千，隨文靜而至，又獻馬千匹。

translations.literal: Shibi was greatly pleased and at once sent General Kang Shaoli leading two thousand horsemen to follow Wenjing; he also presented a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi was delighted and sent General Kang Shaoli with two thousand horsemen, plus a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，謂文靜曰：「非公善辭，何以致此？

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and told Wenjing: "If not for your skilled words, how could this have been achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was overjoyed and told Wenjing: "Without your eloquence, how could we have gained this?"

sentences.zh: 」尋率兵御隋將屈突通於潼關，通遣武牙郎將桑顯和率勁兵來擊，文靜苦戰者半日，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Shortly he led troops to face Sui General Qu Tutong at Tong Pass; Tutong sent Martial-Fang Lang General Sang Xianhe with crack troops to attack; Wenjing fought bitterly for half a day and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon faced Qu Tutong at Tong Pass. Tutong sent Sang Xianhe with crack troops; Wenjing fought half a day and lost thousands.

sentences.zh: 文靜度顯和軍稍怠，潛遣奇兵掩其後，顯和大敗，悉虜其眾。

translations.literal: Wenjing judged Xianhe's army slightly slackened and secretly sent odd troops to strike his rear; Xianhe was utterly defeated and all his troops were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing saw Xianhe's line slacken and sent flanking troops; Xianhe was crushed and his force captured entire.

sentences.zh: 通尚擁兵數萬，將遁歸東都，文靜遣諸將追而執之，略定新安以西之地。

translations.literal: Tutong still held several tens of thousands of troops and wished to flee back to the Eastern Capital; Wenjing sent generals in pursuit to seize him and broadly pacified the lands west of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong still held tens of thousands and meant to flee east; Wenjing's generals pursued, seized him, and pacified the lands west of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 轉大丞相府司馬，進授光祿大夫，封魯國公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Major of the Grand Chancellor's Directorate, advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He became Major of the Grand Chancellor's Directorate, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜納言。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Wenjing was appointed Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Wenjing was appointed Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時高祖每引重臣共食，文靜奏曰：「陛下君臨億兆，率土莫非臣，而當朝捴抑，言尚稱名；

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu often ate with great ministers; Wenjing memorialized: "Your Majesty rules the hundred millions—all within the soil are your subjects—yet at court you suppress them and in speech still use personal names;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often dined with great ministers. Wenjing memorialized: "Your Majesty rules all under Heaven, yet at court you still call ministers by name;

sentences.zh: 又宸極位尊，帝座嚴重，乃使太陽俯同萬物，臣下震恐，無以措身。

translations.literal: moreover the imperial pole is exalted and the throne august—yet you make the sun bow level with the myriad things; ministers below are terrified and have nowhere to place themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "the throne is august—yet you make the sun bow to common things. Your servants are terrified and cannot comport themselves."

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 時制度草創，命文靜與當朝通識之士更刊《隋開皇律令》而損益之，以為通法。

translations.literal: As institutions were newly founded, Gaozu ordered Wenjing with knowledgeable men of the court to revise the Sui Kaihuang codes and statutes with additions and deletions to serve as the general law.
translations.idiomatic: As institutions were being founded, Gaozu ordered Wenjing and knowledgeable courtiers to revise the Sui Kaihuang codes into a general law.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂曰：「本設法令，使人共解，而往代相承，多為隱語，執法之官，緣此舞弄。

translations.literal: Gaozu told him: "Laws and orders were originally set so people could understand them together, but former ages handed them down mostly as hidden language, and executing officers twisted them thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Laws were meant to be understood by all, but former ages handed down hidden language so officers could twist them."

sentences.zh: 宜更刊定，務使易知。

translations.literal: They should be newly edited and made easy to know."
translations.idiomatic: "Edit them anew and make them plain."

sentences.zh: 」會薛舉寇涇州，命太宗討之，以文靜為元帥府長史。

translations.literal: When Xue Ju raided Jing Prefecture, Gaozu ordered Taizong to campaign against him and made Wenjing Chief Clerk of the Commander's Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju raided Jing Prefecture, Gaozu sent Taizong against him with Wenjing as Chief Clerk of the Commander's Directorate.

sentences.zh: 遇太宗不豫，委於文靜及司馬殷開山，誡之曰：「舉糧少兵疲，懸軍深入，意在決戰，不利持久，即欲挑戰，慎無與決。

translations.literal: When Taizong fell ill, he entrusted matters to Wenjing and Major Yin Kaishan, instructing them: "Ju has little grain and weary troops, his army deep in enemy country intent on decisive battle and ill suited to a long stand—if you wish to offer battle, beware deciding with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong fell ill he entrusted command to Wenjing and Major Yin Kaishan: "Ju has little grain and weary troops far from home, eager for battle and ill suited to delay. If you offer battle, do not decide the issue with him.

sentences.zh: 待吾差，當為君等取之。

translations.literal: Wait until I am somewhat recovered and I will take him for you."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until I recover and I will take him for you."

sentences.zh: 」文靜用開山計，出軍爭利，王師敗績。

translations.literal: Wenjing used Kaishan's plan, led the army to contend for gain, and the imperial army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing followed Kaishan's plan, fought for advantage, and the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 文靜奔還京師，坐除名。

translations.literal: Wenjing fled back to the capital and was punished by removal from name.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing fled to the capital and was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 俄又從太宗討舉，平之，以功復其爵邑，拜民部尚書，領陝東道行台左僕射。

translations.literal: Shortly he again followed Taizong in campaigning against Ju and pacified him; for merit his title and fief were restored and he was appointed Minister of the People and Left Vice Minister of the Shandong East Route Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Taizong against Ju, pacified him, and had his title and fief restored; he became Minister of the People and Left Vice Minister on the Shandong East Route.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，從太宗鎮長春宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he followed Taizong in garrisoning Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 2 he followed Taizong in garrisoning Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 文靜自以才能幹用在裴寂之右，又屢有軍功，而位居其下，意甚不平。

translations.literal: Wenjing considered his talent and capacity above Pei Ji's and had repeatedly won military achievement, yet his rank stood below—his mind was very unbalanced.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing thought himself more capable than Pei Ji and had won repeated victories, yet stood below him—he was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 每廷議多相違戾，寂有所是，文靜必非之，由是與寂有隙。

translations.literal: In court deliberations he often opposed Ji; whatever Ji approved, Wenjing was sure to reject—therefore he had a rift with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In council he often opposed Ji; whatever Ji approved, Wenjing rejected—so a rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 文靜嘗與其弟通直散騎常侍文起酣宴，出言怨望，拔刀擊柱曰：「必當斬裴寂耳！

translations.literal: Wenjing once feasted deeply with his younger brother, Regular Attendant Wenqi, speaking words of resentment, and struck a pillar with his sword, saying: "I must cut off Pei Ji's head!
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing once drank deeply with his brother Wenqi, spoke in resentment, and struck a pillar with his sword: "I will cut off Pei Ji's head!"

sentences.zh: 」家中妖怪數見，文起憂之，遂召巫者於星下被髮銜刀，為厭勝之法。

translations.literal: Strange apparitions appeared several times in the house; Wenqi was troubled and therefore summoned a shaman under the stars with hair unbound holding a knife to perform exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: Strange apparitions appeared in the house; Wenqi summoned a shaman under the stars with hair unbound and a knife in his mouth to perform exorcism.

sentences.zh: 時文靜有愛妾失寵，以狀告其兄，妾兄上變。

translations.literal: At that time Wenjing had a favored concubine who lost favor and reported the matter to her elder brother; the concubine's brother submitted a report of treason.
translations.idiomatic: A favored concubine who had lost favor reported the affair to her brother; he submitted a treason report.

sentences.zh: 高祖以之屬吏，遣裴寂、蕭瑀問狀。

translations.literal: Gaozu handed him to the officials and sent Pei Ji and Xiao Yu to examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu handed him to the judiciary and sent Pei Ji and Xiao Yu to examine the case.

sentences.zh: 文靜曰：「起義之初，忝為司馬，計與長史位望略同；

translations.literal: Wenjing said: "At the start of the righteous rising I was honored as Army Major; in planning, my rank and the Chief Clerk's standing were roughly equal;
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing said: "At the founding I was Army Major, roughly equal to the Chief Clerk in standing;

sentences.zh: 今寂為僕射，據甲第，臣官賞不異眾人，東西征討，家口無托，實有觖望之心。

translations.literal: now Ji is Vice Minister and occupies a first-rank mansion while my office and rewards are no different from the multitude; campaigning east and west, my household has no support—truly I had a mind of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: "now Ji is Vice Minister in a first-rank mansion while my rewards match the common run; I campaigned east and west while my household went unsupported—I did resent it.

sentences.zh: 因醉或有怨言，不能自保。

translations.literal: Through wine I sometimes had complaining words and could not preserve myself."
translations.idiomatic: In wine I sometimes spoke bitterly and could not guard my tongue."

sentences.zh: 」高祖謂群臣曰：「文靜此言，反明白矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu told the ministers: "Wenjing's words are plainly rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told the ministers: "Wenjing's own words are open rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」李綱、蕭瑀皆明其非反。

translations.literal: Li Gang and Xiao Yu both made clear he was not rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang and Xiao Yu both argued he was not rebelling.

sentences.zh: 太宗以文靜義旗初起，先定非常之策，始告寂知；

translations.literal: Taizong, because at the start of the righteous banner Wenjing first settled the extraordinary design and first told Ji,
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, because Wenjing had first shaped the founding design and first told Ji,

sentences.zh: 及平京城，任遇懸隔，止以文靜為觖望，非敢謀反，極佑助之。

translations.literal: and when the capital was pacified treatment and rank were far apart—only that Wenjing resented—did not dare rebel, and pleaded for him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: and because rewards after the capital fell were unequal—argued it was resentment only, not rebellion—and pleaded for him to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 而高祖素疏忌之，裴寂又言曰：「文靜才略，實冠時人，性復粗險，忿不思難，丑言悖逆，其狀已彰。

translations.literal: But Gaozu had long been distant and suspicious toward him, and Pei Ji also said: "Wenjing's talent and strategy truly crown the age; his nature is again coarse and dangerous—anger without thought of difficulty, ugly words rebellious—his condition is already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: But Gaozu had long distrusted him, and Pei Ji said: "Wenjing's talent crowns the age, yet he is coarse and rash, speaking rebellious words in anger—the case is clear.

sentences.zh: 當今天下未定，外有勍敵，今若赦之，必貽後患。

translations.literal: Now the realm is not yet settled and there are strong enemies outside—if we pardon him now, we will surely leave trouble for later."
translations.idiomatic: "The realm is not settled and strong enemies remain—pardon him now and trouble follows."

sentences.zh: 」高祖竟聽其言，遂殺文靜、文起，仍籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Gaozu finally listened and killed Wenjing and Wenqi, and still confiscated their household.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu listened and executed Wenjing and Wenqi, confiscating their property.

sentences.zh: 文靜臨刑，撫膺嘆曰：「高鳥逝，良弓藏，故不虛也。

translations.literal: Facing execution, Wenjing clutched his breast and sighed: "When the high bird goes, the good bow is stored—how true the saying.
translations.idiomatic: At execution Wenjing clutched his breast and sighed: "When the high bird goes, the good bow is stored—how true."

sentences.zh: 」時年五十二。

translations.literal: He was fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，追復官爵，以子樹義襲封魯國公，許尚公主。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan his office and title were posthumously restored; his son Shuyi inherited as Duke of Lu and was permitted to marry a princess.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 3 his office and title were restored; his son Shuyi inherited as Duke of Lu and was permitted to marry a princess.

sentences.zh: 後與其兄樹藝怨其父被戮，又謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Later he and his elder brother Shuyi resented their father's execution and again plotted rebellion; they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and his brother Shuyi, resenting their father's execution, rebelled again and were executed.

sentences.zh: 文靜初為納言時，有詔以太原元謀立功，尚書令、秦王某，尚書左僕射裴寂及文靜，特恕二死。

translations.literal: When Wenjing first became Master of Writing, there was an edict that for original merit in plotting at Taiyuan, the Minister Director and a certain Prince of Qin, Left Vice Minister Pei Ji and Wenjing, were specially pardoned twice from death.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjing first became Master of Writing, an edict pardoned twice from death the Minister Director, a certain Prince of Qin, Left Vice Minister Pei Ji, and Wenjing for their original Taiyuan plotting.

sentences.zh: 左驍衛大將軍長孫順德、右驍衛大將軍劉弘基、右屯衛大將軍竇琮、左翊衛大將軍柴紹、內史侍郎唐儉、吏部侍郎殷開山、鴻臚卿劉世龍、衛尉少卿劉政會、都水監趙文恪、庫部郎中武士鸊、驃騎將軍張平高、李思行、李高遷，左屯衛府長史許世緒等十四人，約免一死。

translations.literal: Left Illustrious Martial General Zhangsun Shunde, Right Illustrious Martial General Liu Hongji, Right Stationing Martial General Dou Cong, Left Wing Guard General Chai Shao, Palace Secretariat Vice Minister Tang Jian, Ministry Vice Minister Yin Kaishan, Chamberlain Liu Shilong, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Vice Minister Liu Zhenghui, Directorate of Waterways Supervisor Zhao Wenge, Warehouse Bureau Gentleman Wu Shiyi, Flying Cavalry General Zhang Pinggao, Li Sixing, Li Gaogian, and Left Stationing Guard Directorate Chief Clerk Xu Shiji—fourteen men in all—were pledged one pardon from death.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen others—including Zhangsun Shunde, Liu Hongji, Dou Cong, Chai Shao, Tang Jian, Yin Kaishan, Liu Shilong, Liu Zhenghui, Zhao Wenge, Wu Shiyi, Zhang Pinggao, Li Sixing, Li Gaogian, and Xu Shiji—were pledged one pardon from death.

sentences.zh: 武德九年十月，太宗始定功臣實封差第，文靜已死，於是裴寂加食九百戶，通前為一千五百戶；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year of Wude, Taizong first fixed the graded substantive fiefs of merit subjects; Wenjing was already dead—thereupon Pei Ji's fief was increased by nine hundred households, nine hundred added to the previous total of one thousand five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 9, month 10, Taizong fixed graded merit fiefs. Wenjing was dead; Pei Ji's fief rose by nine hundred households to fifteen hundred in all;

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、王君廓、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦等五人，食邑一千三百戶；

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, Wang Junguo, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and five others had fiefs of one thousand three hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, Wang Junguo, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and five others received thirteen hundred households;

sentences.zh: 長孫順德、柴紹、羅藝、趙郡王孝恭等四人，食邑一千二百戶；

translations.literal: Zhangsun Shunde, Chai Shao, Luo Yi, Prince Xiaogong of Zhao, and four others had one thousand two hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shunde, Chai Shao, Luo Yi, Prince Xiaogong of Zhao, and four others received twelve hundred;

sentences.zh: 侯君集、張公謹、劉師立等三人食邑一千戶；

translations.literal: Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Liu Shili, and three others had one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Liu Shili, and three others received one thousand;

sentences.zh: 李勣、劉弘基二人食邑九百戶；

translations.literal: Li Ji and Liu Hongji had nine hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji and Liu Hongji received nine hundred;

sentences.zh: 高士廉、宇文士及、秦叔寶、程知節四人食七百戶；

translations.literal: Gao Shilian, Yuwen Shiji, Qin Shubao, and Cheng Yaohua had seven hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian, Yuwen Shiji, Qin Shubao, and Cheng Yaohua received seven hundred;

sentences.zh: 安興貴、安修仁、唐儉、竇軌、屈突通、蕭瑀、封德彝、劉義節八人，各食六百戶；

translations.literal: An Xinggui, An Xiuren, Tang Jian, Dou Gui, Qu Tutong, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and Liu Yijie—eight men—each had six hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui, An Xiuren, Tang Jian, Dou Gui, Qu Tutong, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and Liu Yijie—eight men—each received six hundred;

sentences.zh: 錢九隴、樊興、公孫武達、李孟嘗、段志玄、龐卿惲、張亮、李藥師、杜淹、元仲文十人，各食四百戶；

translations.literal: Qian Jiulong, Fan Xing, Gongsun Wuda, Li Mengchang, Duan Zhixuan, Pang Qingyun, Zhang Liang, Li Yaoshi, Du Yan, and Yuan Zhongwen—ten men—each had four hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jiulong, Fan Xing, Gongsun Wuda, Li Mengchang, Duan Zhixuan, Pang Qingyun, Zhang Liang, Li Yaoshi, Du Yan, and Yuan Zhongwen—ten men—each received four hundred;

sentences.zh: 張長遜、張平高、李安遠、李子和、秦行師、馬三寶六人，各食三百戶。

translations.literal: Zhang Changsun, Zhang Pinggao, Li Anyuan, Li Zihe, Qin Xingshi, and Ma Sanbao—six men—each had three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changsun, Zhang Pinggao, Li Anyuan, Li Zihe, Qin Xingshi, and Ma Sanbao—six men—each received three hundred.

sentences.zh: 其王君廓事在《廬江王瑗傳》，安興貴、安修仁事在《李軌傳》，李子和事在《梁師都傳》，馬三寶事在《柴紹傳》。

translations.literal: Wang Junguo's affair is in the biography of Prince Yuan of Lujiang; An Xinggui and An Xiuren are in the biography of Li Gui; Li Zihe is in the biography of Liang Shidu; Ma Sanbao is in the biography of Chai Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junguo appears in the biography of Prince Yuan of Lujiang; An Xinggui and An Xiuren in Li Gui's biography; Li Zihe in Liang Shidu's; Ma Sanbao in Chai Shao's.

sentences.zh: 李孟嘗 秦行師李孟嘗，趙州平棘人，官至右威衛大將軍、漢東郡公。

translations.literal: Li Mengchang and Qin Xingshi. Li Mengchang was a man of Pingji in Zhao Prefecture; he reached Right Majestic Guard General and Duke of Handong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengchang and Qin Xingshi. Li Mengchang of Pingji in Zhao Prefecture rose to Right Majestic Guard General and Duke of Handong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元仲文，洛州人，至右監門將軍、河南縣公。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhongwen was a man of Luozhou; he reached Right Gate Guard General and Duke of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhongwen of Luozhou became Right Gate Guard General and Duke of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 秦行師，并州太原人，至左監門將軍、清水郡公。

translations.literal: Qin Xingshi was a man of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture; he reached Left Gate Guard General and Duke of Qingshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xingshi of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture became Left Gate Guard General and Duke of Qingshui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 並事微不錄。

translations.literal: Their affairs were slight and are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds were slight and are not recorded separately.

sentences.zh: 自余無傳者，盡附於此。

translations.literal: Those without biographies are all appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Those without separate biographies are gathered here.

sentences.zh: 劉世龍劉世龍者，并州晉陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong. Liu Shilong was a man of Jinyang in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong came from Jinyang in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為晉陽鄉長。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he was District Elder of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he was District Elder of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，裴寂數薦之，由是甚見接待，亦出入王威、高君雅家，然獨歸心於高祖。

translations.literal: When Gaozu garrisoned Taiyuan, Pei Ji repeatedly recommended him; he was therefore greatly received, and also went in and out of the houses of Wang Wei and Gao Junya, yet his heart alone turned to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu garrisoned Taiyuan, Pei Ji repeatedly recommended him; he was well received and even moved in Wang Wei and Gao Junya's circles, yet his loyalty was Gaozu's alone.

sentences.zh: 義兵將起，威與君雅內懷疑惑，世龍輒探得其情，以白高祖。

translations.literal: When the righteous army was about to rise, Wei and Junya harbored doubts within; Shilong always probed their intentions and reported to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: As the righteous army was about to rise, Wei and Junya harbored doubts; Shilong probed their intentions and reported to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 及誅威等，授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Wei and the others were executed, he was made Silver-Green Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei and Junya were executed he was made Silver-Green Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從平京城，累轉鴻臚卿，仍改名義節。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the capital he was repeatedly transferred to Chamberlain and then renamed Yijie.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell he rose to Chamberlain and was renamed Yijie.

sentences.zh: 時草創之始，傾竭府藏以賜勳人，而國用不足，義節進計曰：「今義師數萬，並在京師，樵薪貴而布帛賤。

translations.literal: At the start of founding, the treasury was drained to reward merit men while state use was insufficient; Yijie advanced a plan, saying: "Now the righteous army numbers tens of thousands, all in the capital; firewood is costly and cloth cheap."
translations.idiomatic: At the founding the treasury was drained rewarding merit men while revenue failed; Yijie proposed: "Tens of thousands of the righteous army are in the capital; firewood is costly and cloth cheap."

sentences.zh: 若采街衢及苑中樹為樵以易布帛，歲收數十萬匹立可致也。

translations.literal: If trees along streets and in the parks are taken as firewood to exchange for cloth, several hundred thousand lengths can be obtained at once.
translations.idiomatic: "Cut street and park trees for firewood to exchange for cloth, and hundreds of thousands of lengths can be had at once."

sentences.zh: 又藏內繒絹，匹匹軸之，使申截取剩物，以供雜費，動盈十餘萬段矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, stored silks in the vaults, each bolt on its roller—if cut to reclaim remnants for miscellaneous expenses, more than a hundred thousand lengths are easily gained.
translations.idiomatic: "Stored silks on their rollers—trim remnants for miscellaneous expenses—and more than a hundred thousand lengths follow."

sentences.zh: 」高祖並從之，大收其利。

translations.literal: Gaozu followed both and greatly collected the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu adopted both measures and reaped great profit.

sentences.zh: 再遷太府卿，封葛國公。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of the Palace and enfeoffed as Duke of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Minister of the Palace and enfeoffed Duke of Ge.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，轉少府監，以罪配流嶺南，尋授欽州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: In early Zhenguan he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Palace and, for a crime, was sentenced to exile in Lingnan; shortly he was made Vice Prefect of Qin Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhenguan he became Vice Minister of the Palace, was exiled to Lingnan for a crime, then made Vice Prefect of Qin and died.

sentences.zh: 義節從子思禮，萬歲通天二年，為箕州刺史。

translations.literal: Yijie's nephew by younger brother's line Silun, in the second year of Wansui Tongtian, was Prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie's nephew Silun, in Wansui Tongtian year 2, was Prefect of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思禮少嘗學相術於許州張憬藏，相己必歷刺史，位至太師。

translations.literal: Silun in youth had studied physiognomy under Zhang Jingzang of Xu Prefecture; reading his own face he was sure to reach prefect and rise to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Silun had studied physiognomy under Zhang Jingzang of Xu and read in his own face that he would reach prefect and rise to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 及授箕州，益自喜，以為太師之職，位極人臣，非佐命無以致之。

translations.literal: When appointed to Ji Prefecture he was still more pleased, thinking the Grand Preceptor's office—the pinnacle of human subjects—could not be reached without aiding the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed to Ji, he was still more pleased, thinking the Grand Preceptor's rank—the pinnacle of subjects—required aiding the mandate.

sentences.zh: 與洛州錄事參軍綦連耀結構謀反，謂耀曰：「公體有龍氣。

translations.literal: With Qililian Yao, Registrar of Luozhou, he formed a plot of rebellion; he told Yao: "Your body has dragon qi."
translations.idiomatic: With Luozhou Registrar Qililian Yao he plotted rebellion and told Yao: "Your body bears dragon qi."

sentences.zh: 」耀亦謂思禮曰：「公是金刀，合為我輔。

translations.literal: Yao also told Silun: "You, sir, are the Golden Blade and should assist me."
translations.idiomatic: Yao told Silun in turn: "You are the Golden Blade and should assist me."

sentences.zh: 」因相解釋圖讖，即定君臣之契。

translations.literal: They therefore mutually explained charts and prophecies and at once fixed the covenant of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: They interpreted charts and prophecies together and fixed a lord-and-minister covenant.

sentences.zh: 又令思禮自衒相術，每所見人，皆謂之「合得三品」，使務進之士，聞之滿望，然始謂云：「綦連耀有天分，公因之以得富貴。

translations.literal: He also had Silun display physiognomy himself; whomever he saw he told would "surely reach the third rank," making ambitious men hear it with full hope—yet at first he said: "Qililian Yao has Heaven's portion; you, sir, will gain wealth and honor through him."
translations.idiomatic: He had Silun practice physiognomy in public, telling every man he met he would reach the third rank, filling ambitious hearts with hope—while saying Yao had Heaven's portion and Silun would rise through him.

sentences.zh: 」事發繫獄，乃多證引朝士，冀以自免。

translations.literal: When the affair broke he was imprisoned and then implicated many court gentlemen, hoping thereby to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot broke he was imprisoned and implicated many courtiers hoping to save himself.

sentences.zh: 所誅陷者三十餘家，耀、思禮並伏誅。

translations.literal: More than thirty households were framed and executed; Yao and Silun were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty households were framed and executed; Yao and Silun both died.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎李元素、夏官侍郎孫元亨、知天官侍郎事石抱忠、鳳閣舍人王劇、劇兄前涇州刺史勔、太子司議郎路敬淳等，坐與耀及思禮交結，皆死。

translations.literal: Deputy Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Li Yuansu, Summer Official Vice Minister Sun Yuanheng, Shi Baozhong knowing Heaven Official Vice Minister affairs, Phoenix Pavilion Gentleman Wang Ju, Ju's elder brother former Jing Prefecture Prefect Mao, Crown Prince Remonstrating Gentleman Lu Jingchun, and others, for associating with Yao and Silun, all died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuansu, Sun Yuanheng, Shi Baozhong, Wang Ju, Ju's brother former Jing Prefect Mao, Lu Jingchun, and others who associated with Yao and Silun all died.
